svg.text: Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 8 components · 11 data flows · 4 trust boundaries · 71 threats

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-02; tb-2 External → C-03; tb-3 External → C-04; tb-6 C-02 → External

df-002: POST /rest/user/login — credentials submitted for authentication; server returns JWT and basket ID (HTTP) df-003: POST /rest/2fa/verify — TOTP code submitted with temporary token to complete MFA login (HTTP) df-002 authentication: Login endpoint requires no prior authentication; credentials are the request payload; evidence: routes/login.ts:18 df-002 access group: Password then TOTP if 2FA enrolled; sequence; step 1 df-003 authentication: Temporary token issued by the login handler when TOTP is required; carries userId and type totp_token_required; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:20 df-003 access group: Password then TOTP if 2FA enrolled; sequence; step 2

df-004: Authenticated REST API requests carrying JWT Bearer token for protected resources (HTTP) df-005: Unauthenticated REST API requests for public endpoints such as product listing and search (HTTP) df-004 authentication: JWT token retrieved from localStorage and injected by request interceptor into Authorization header; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:13, lib/insecurity.ts:156 df-004 access group: Authenticated or anonymous API access; alternatives; step n/a df-005 authentication: No authentication required; routes serve public data or are missing auth by design; evidence: server.ts:182 df-005 access group: Authenticated or anonymous API access; alternatives; step n/a

df-006: Sequelize ORM queries reading and writing user accounts, orders, basket items, feedback, and payment cards (SQLite) df-006 authentication: SQLite is a local file-based database with no network authentication layer; evidence: models/index.ts:33

df-007: MarsDB collection queries for product reviews and orders documents (MarsDB) df-007 authentication: MarsDB is an in-process embedded store with no authentication layer; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-008: Socket.IO WebSocket connection for receiving real-time challenge-solved and server-start notifications (WebSocket) df-008 authentication: No JWT or session check located in the Socket.IO connection handler; evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-009: OAuth 2.0 implicit-flow authorization redirect to Google; access token returned in URL fragment (HTTPS) df-009 authentication: Browser-only implicit flow with response_type=token; no state parameter; no server-side token exchange; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148

df-010: LLM chat completion request to Ollama endpoint via @ai-sdk/openai-compatible SDK (HTTP) df-010 authentication: API URL loaded from config; no API key or auth token observed in routes/chat.ts initialization; evidence: routes/chat.ts:109
df-011: User input; evidence: frontend/src/app/app.routing.ts:81, frontend/src/app/app.guard.ts:48

End user running the Angular SPA in a web browser. After login, carries a JWT bearer token in localStorage attached to API requests by the HTTP interceptor.

g.title: Google authorization endpoint used by the Angular login component for OAuth 2.0 implicit-flow sign-in. The browser is redirected to Google and receives the access token directly in the URL fragment.
g.text: the Angular login component for OAuth

g.title: External LLM endpoint (Ollama at localhost:11434 or configurable remote URL) called by routes/chat.ts via the @ai-sdk/openai-compatible SDK. Used for the AI chatbot challenge.

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
A1 ①② = scenarios of attacker A1 · A1 at an arrowhead = its attack
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
